operations.before:
Assume Countable Choice and the conforming Galerkin setting of
[[thm-cea-quasi-optimality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations]]. Let
$H=L^2(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with inner product linear in the first slot, and
let $J:V\to H$ be a continuous linear inclusion with
$\|Jv\|_H\le C_E\|v\|_V$. Put $e:=J(u-u_h)$. The adjoint solution $z_e$ is
the unique element of $V$ satisfying
$$a(v,z_e)=(Jv,e)_H\qquad(v\in V);$$
it exists by [[thm-adjoint-problem-for-bounded-coercive-variational-forms]].
Let $s\in(0,1]$, and let $R_s\subseteq V$ be a specified normed space of
adjoint-regular functions. Assume constants $C_R,C_I$ independent of $h$ and
the error satisfy
$$\|z_e\|_{R_s}\le C_R\|e\|_H,\qquad \inf_{w_h\in V_h}\|z_e-w_h\|_V\le C_Ih^s\|z_e\|_{R_s}.$$
Then
$$\|u-u_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le M C_I C_R h^s\|u-u_h\|_V.$$
The symbol $R_s$ means exactly the chosen regularity norm space in the two
displayed assumptions; no fractional Sobolev interpolation estimate is
asserted unless it verifies the second inequality. The integer endpoint may
be instantiated with $R_1=H^2(\Omega)=W^{2,2}(\Omega)$.

before.quote:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a
bounded polyhedral open set with a matching shape-regular affine simplicial
mesh family $\{\mathcal T_h\}$, and set $h:=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K\le1$.
Fix an integer $r\ge1$. On the reference simplex let
$(\widehat S_d,\widehat P,\widehat\Sigma)$ be an unisolvent real scalar
finite element whose finite-dimensional local space $\widehat P$ consists of
polynomials and contains $\mathbb P_r$. Assume each
degree of freedom has a bounded linear extension to
$W^{r+1,2}(\widehat S_d)$, and let $\widehat I$ be its interpolant. Suppose
there is a global map $I_h$ whose restriction to each cell is the affine
pullback of $\widehat I$, and that $I_hu\in V_h$ for the conforming discrete
space $V_h\subset H^1_0(\Omega)$ whenever
$u\in W^{r+1,2}(\Omega)\cap H^1_0(\Omega)$, where $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is the
closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ in $W^{1,2}(\Omega)$
([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]). Then a constant $C$ independent of
$h$ and $u$ satisfies
$$\|u-I_hu\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C h^r|u|_{W^{r+1,2}(\Omega)}.$$
The global conformity and zero-boundary mapping property of $I_h$ are explicit
hypotheses; this estimate does not assert them for arbitrary degrees of
freedom.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and let
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ be linear in its first argument, conjugate-linear
in its second, bounded by $M$, and coercive with constant $\alpha>0$:
$$|a(v,w)|\le M\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad \operatorname{Re}a(v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2.$$
Let $F:V\to\mathbb K$ be bounded and conjugate-linear, and let $V_h\subseteq V$
be finite-dimensional. Then there are unique $u\in V$ and $u_h\in V_h$ with
$$a(u,v)=F(v)\quad(v\in V).$$
$$a(u_h,v_h)=F(v_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h).$$
The solutions satisfy
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac M\alpha\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.$$
The real bilinear case uses linear functionals and reads $\operatorname{Re}$ as
the identity.

Assume Countable Choice and the conforming Galerkin setting of

$\|Jv\|_H\le C_E\|v\|_V$. Put $e:=J(u-u_h)$. The adjoint solution $z_e$ is
the unique element of $V$ satisfying
$$a(v,z_e)=(Jv,e)_H\qquad(v\in V);$$
it exists by [[thm-adjoint-problem-for-bounded-coercive-variational-forms]].
Let $s\in(0,1]$, and let $R_s\subseteq V$ be a specified normed space of
adjoint-regular functions. Assume constants $C_R,C_I$ independent of $h$ and
the error satisfy
$$\|z_e\|_{R_s}\le C_R\|e\|_H,\qquad \inf_{w_h\in V_h}\|z_e-w_h\|_V\le C_Ih^s\|z_e\|_{R_s}.$$
Then
$$\|u-u_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le M C_I C_R h^s\|u-u_h\|_V.$$
The symbol $R_s$ means exactly the chosen regularity norm space in the two
displayed assumptions; no fractional Sobolev interpolation estimate is
asserted unless it verifies the second inequality. The integer endpoint may
be instantiated with $R_1=H^2(\Omega)\cap V$, using the
$H^2(\Omega)=W^{2,2}(\Omega)$ norm. If $H^2(\Omega)\subseteq V$,
this is simply $R_1=H^2(\Omega)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. On $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]) define $$(u,v)_{H^1}:=(u,v)_{L^2}+\sum_{i=1}^n(D_iu,D_iv)_{L^2},$$ with the $L^2$ inner product of [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. Then $(\cdot,\cdot)_{H^1}$ is an inner product on the Sobolev classes whose induced norm is the $W^{1,2}$ norm of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and $H^1(\Omega)$ is a Hilbert space for it. The zero-boundary space $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a closed subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]) and hence a Hilbert space for the restricted inner product. The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, in the convention of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]].

operations.before: Apply the Aubin–Nitsche estimate [F3] with $V=H^1_0(\Omega)$ in its $H^1$ norm, $C_I=C_D$, and the two dual bounds [A1]. This gives $\|u-u_h\|_{L^2}\le M C_DC_Rh^s\|u-u_h\|_{H^1}$.
operations.after: By [F4], $V=H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a Hilbert space in its stated $H^1$ norm. Apply the Aubin–Nitsche estimate [F3] with $V=H^1_0(\Omega)$ in its $H^1$ norm, $C_I=C_D$, and the two dual bounds [A1]. This gives $\|u-u_h\|_{L^2}\le M C_DC_Rh^s\|u-u_h\|_{H^1}$.

operations.before: Apply [F2] to the best-approximation bound in step 1.1. This gives $\|u-u_h\|_{H^1}\le \frac M\alpha C_{\rm FE}h^r|u|_{W^{r+1,2}}.$
operations.after: Apply [F2] on the Hilbert space supplied by [F4] to the best-approximation bound in step 1.1. This gives $\|u-u_h\|_{H^1}\le \frac M\alpha C_{\rm FE}h^r|u|_{W^{r+1,2}}.$
